primary_meaning: Spiritual humility and total dependence on God (the 'anawim' ideal): those who recognize their own spiritual poverty/need and meekly trust God rather than wealth, power, or self-sufficiency
primary_basis: Psalm 37:11 and related Psalms (meek/anawim inherit the land)
Isaiah 61:1 / Luke 4:18 (good news to the poor)
Zephaniah 2:3; 3:12 (humble and lowly who seek the Lord)
Luke 1:46-55 (Magnificat theme of God lifting the lowly)

alternatives.meaning: Primarily or exclusively material/economic poverty as a condition specially favored or blessed by God
The oppressed faithful remnant of Israel (or the Church) awaiting eschatological vindication
basis: OT anawim motif across Psalms and prophets

alternatives.meaning: Mere gentleness of temperament without reference to spiritual need or socioeconomic status

notes: Traditional Christian exegesis (patristic through Reformation and most modern confessional teaching) consistently privileges the spiritual-humility reading while still allowing secondary material or social applications; pure economic-only readings remain secondary in the broader historical consensus.
